paper.title: Learning prices for repeated auctions with strategic buyers

settings.name_in_paper: Fixed Value Setting (repeated posted-price auction with strategic buyer)
unmapped: Buyer is strategic: knows the seller's announced algorithm and maximizes her discounted surplus
Buyer has a single fixed value v in (0,1]; seller posts prices in [0,1], observes only accept/reject
Geometric buyer discount gamma_t = gamma^(t-1); regret measured against best fixed price with a truthful buyer (strategic regret)
settings.definition_quote: In this section we consider the case of a single unknown fixed buyer value, that is $\CV = \{v\}$ for some $v \in (0, 1]$.

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic Value Setting (finite price set, strategic buyer)
unmapped: Buyer is strategic (surplus-maximizing against the announced algorithm), with geometric discount gamma_t = gamma^(t-1)
Buyer values v_t i.i.d. from D on [0,1] with K-Lipschitz survival function F(p)=Pr[v>=p]
Arms are prices in a finite set P (K = |P|); reward is p * 1{accept}; regret against best fixed price with truthful buyer
settings.definition_quote: We next give a seller algorithm that attains no-regret when the set of prices $\CP$ is finite, the buyer's discount is $\gamma_t = \gamma^{t-1}$, and the buyer's value $v_t$ for each round is drawn from a fixed distribution $\CD$ that satistfies a certain continuity assumption

settings.name_in_paper: Repeated posted-price auction with strategic buyer (lower bound)
unmapped: Strategic surplus-maximizing buyer with arbitrary positive nonincreasing discount sequence gamma_t; T_gamma = sum_t gamma_t
Regret measured against best fixed price with a truthful buyer (strategic regret)
settings.definition_quote: Associated with the buyer is a fixed distribution $\mathcal{D}$ over the interval $[0,1]$, which is known only to the buyer. On each round $t$, the buyer receives a value $v_t \in \CV \subseteq [0,1]$ from the distribution $\mathcal{D}$. The seller, without observing this value, then posts a price $p_t \in \CP \subseteq [0,1]$.

results.notes: Strategic regret = T p* F(p*) - expected revenue, mapped to pseudo_regret. Algorithm itself with fixed beta does not need T; marked known horizon loosely.

source.label: thm:tuned
source.quote: If $\beta = \frac{\sqrt{T}}{1+\sqrt{T}}$ ~then ~$\regret(\CAm, v, T) \le \sqrt{T} \left( 4 v T_\gamma + 2 v \log\left(\frac{1}{v}\right) \right) + v$

results.notes: Tuning does not require knowledge of gamma, but needs T.

bound.expression_latex: c_1 |\CP| T^\alpha + c_2\frac{|\CP|^2}{\Delta^{2/\alpha}} (\log T)^{1/\alpha} + c_3 \frac{|\CP|^2}{\Delta^{1/\alpha}} T_\gamma^{1/\alpha}(\log T + \log(K/\Delta))^{1/\alpha} + c_4|\CP| = \tilde{O}(T^\alpha + T_\gamma^{1/\alpha})

source.label: thm:phasedbound

results.notes: Constants c1..c4 unspecified (may depend on alpha), so recorded as O. Paper's K (Lipschitz) renamed K_lip; |P| mapped to K. Also stated as O~(T^alpha + T_gamma^(1/alpha)). Phased uses doubling, does not need T.

conditions: hard instance is a point-mass value distribution

source.label: thm:mainlower
source.quote: Fix a positive, nonincreasing, discount sequence $\{\gamma_t\}$. Let $\CA$ be any seller algorithm for the repeated setting. There exists a buyer value distribution $\CD$ such that $\regret(\CA, \mathcal{D}, T) \geq \frac{1}{12}T_\gamma$. In particular, if $T_\gamma = \Omega(T)$, no-regret is impossible.

results.notes: Proved via reduction to single-shot auction (Lemma 3).
